messages:
Maya: quick Q — rotated the API key in prod and a few Node streaming clients inside Docker started getting 401s and never reconnecting. We mount the key at /etc/redwood/api_key and our app reads it at startup. Anyone seen streams not pick up a rotated key?
Samir: do you reload the in-memory auth header when the file changes? the SDK won't watch files for you automatically.
Maya: we do an fs.watch and reload the token; regular REST requests pick up the new key fine, only the long-lived streaming sessions keep failing with 401 on reconnect.
Lucy: which SDK + transport are you on? http2 / grpc can stash metadata at session create.
Maya: @redwood/sdk-node 0.12.3, using the streaming API over http2.
Samir: common gotcha: if you build an Authorization header at client init and the http2 session is reused, that metadata stays. Recreating the client on rotation usually fixes it. Also how do you write/rotate the file inside the container?
Maya: rotation is atomic on the host (write tmp + mv) and the file in the container is a bind-mounted file provided by swarm/compose as a symlink to /run/secrets/... On mac with osxfs we've seen inode replacement not trigger fs.watch reliably.
Samir: yep — inode change vs content change matters. fs.watch on many platforms only notices content writes not an atomic mv that swaps the inode. Polling the file or watching the parent directory for rename events is more reliable.
Maya: snippet of how we're building the header currently: ```js
const key = fs.readFileSync('/etc/redwood/api_key', 'utf8').trim();
const auth = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`${key}:`).toString('base64');
client = new RedwoodClient({ headers: { Authorization: auth } })
```
Lucy: two quick notes: 1) using `Basic` with an empty username means you append `:` — some HTTP stacks treat that differently vs a `Bearer` token. 2) http2/grpc metadata is captured when the session is created; you need to recreate the client or session to pick up a new header.
Samir: on top of that, if rotation writes a file with different perms or via symlink swap, some runtimes won't follow the new inode. For Docker secrets it's often safer to read the secret at call-time or implement a small watcher that polls the file mtime/inode and then tears down+recreates the streaming client.
Maya: switched to `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and implemented a recreate-on-rotate path (detect inode change + client.close() + new RedwoodClient()). That immediately fixed reconnects.
Lucy: filing an SDK issue to make streaming clients easier to refresh (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/issues/412) and add a line in the runbook recommending `Bearer` for API keys and to recreate streaming clients on rotate.
Maya: will add the runbook note. Thanks — saved me a midnight pagedebug :sweat_smile:

Maya: noted, adding a small test to CI to simulate secret rotate via symlink swap and validate reconnect behavior.
